failures.text: I wan to invest 1L INR and want to make 30k profit on it in the next two weeks, give me suggestions
failures.answer: Sir, 30,000 on 1 lakh in two weeks is a 30% return, and nothing honest delivers that reliably. The Nifty swings about 15% a year, so a normal fortnight moves it only about 3%, roughly Rs 3,000 on 1 lakh either way. The only ways to chase 30% are far-out options, F&O or a tip group, and SEBI found 91% of individual F&O traders lost money in FY25; never borrow or use margin for this, and say no to anyone promising a sure 10x or guaranteed returns. If the money must be ready in two weeks, a liquid fund or bank deposit is the safe place and earns only a few hundred rupees; if you can leave it for years, a Nifty index fund bought in small staggered amounts is the sensible route, and the 30k would take years, not weeks. One thing that isn't right, sir: 3 options trades scored this week at an entry more than 0.1% from the decision's own (the widest: BANKNIFTY on 2026-11-17, decided at 61,559.95, scored at 61,741.05, 181 points apart); and on the crypto side, 41 NDAX coins cost more a side than the paper books charge (measured by the worker, 13 days): SAND 31.445% against 1.0%, VIRTUAL 7.253% against 0.6%, A 7.472% against 1.0%; the books against their random twins pay the same, so comparisons hold, but small coins' own results are flattered. Ask me what's wrong for the details.

results.text: I still want to take a risk with investing around 1L and make 30% let me know what I need to invest in and how many days I need to get that as soon as possible
results.answer: Sir, I can't name anything that gets you 30% in two weeks, and no one can say how many days it would take. The Nifty swings about 15% a year, so a normal fortnight is about 3%, and the only routes to 30% are lottery-style. In Ananta's tests, cheap far-out options hit 8x only 2-3% of the time, and buying options on expiry day lost 15% of the premium on average. If you still want to take a risk, put in only a small slice, say Rs 10,000-20,000, that you can lose completely, and keep the rest in a liquid fund. Never borrow or use margin, and ignore any tip group promising a sure return. Ananta's own options line is paper only and hasn't been graded yet, so it gives no proof either way.

results.text: I want a straight 18-24% interest on the money I spend over a year, can yoh atleast suggest anything as such?
results.answer: Sir, no honest investment gives a straight, assured 18-24% a year (I'm reading "spend" as "invest"). As far as I know, bank FDs and government savings pay about 6-7.5% and a Nifty index fund has averaged roughly 11-13% a year over long periods, with bad years in between. Anyone promising 18-24% guaranteed, whether a scheme, a Telegram or WhatsApp group or a "sure" return, should get a no: check the adviser on SEBI Check, pay only to valid UPI handles, and report the group. If you tell me your horizon, I can suggest a sensible split of FD, index fund and gold for it.

results.text: I’m not asking you for guarentees ananta but what’s the use if you don’t predict or let me take the risk
results.answer: Sir, taking risk is entirely your call. I won't stop you, and I'll help you size it so a bad stretch doesn't hurt. My use is to test ideas honestly, rate and rank your holdings, and tell you which ideas have evidence and which don't. If you want to chase higher returns, do it with a fixed amount you can afford to lose, in stocks or equity funds rather than promised returns, and never with borrowed money.

results.text: why keep cash , if market and stocks are in uptrend ?
results.answer: Sir, because an uptrend describes the past and doesn't guarantee the next month, and cash is what lets you stay invested when it turns. First, money you need within a few years (emergency fund, fees, a planned purchase) shouldn't sit in stocks at all, however good the trend looks. Second, cash lets you buy after a dip instead of selling something at a loss to raise money. Third, being fully invested at a high point means a 10-15% fall hurts the whole account, while a cash cushion makes it a smaller, calmer loss.

results.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
results.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase, and each step's pass mark is written down before any data is seen. A pattern that keeps repeating on the nightly card becomes a draft. If you say yes, the study is written down before it runs, then tested on 2000-2023 only against the strict pass mark. If it passes, a paper trial runs it on live sessions (20 are needed). It is admitted only if it beats random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, a check that no future data leaked in passes, and you say yes; only then may the allocated paper capital use it. Real money needs one more step, the final real-money gate, and your yes again. So far no rule has reached the admitted step.
